capabilityPlanes.title: Regulate & learn
capabilityPlanes.scope: Manage attention, emotion, motivation, recovery, deliberate learning, and correction under real constraints.
outcomes: Reliable retrieval and transfer of learned material
exclusions: Claims that one trait dominates achievement

capabilityPlanes.title: Relate & express
capabilityPlanes.scope: Listen, understand, communicate, speak, facilitate, and build credible connection across people and groups.
outcomes: Useful dialogue in difficult or public settings

capabilityPlanes.title: Sense, decide & create
capabilityPlanes.scope: Observe signals, compare structures, form and test hypotheses, forecast, solve problems, and create useful options.
outcomes: Decisions with visible assumptions and calibration
exclusions: Retrospective certainty without a recorded prediction

capabilityPlanes.title: Lead & coordinate
capabilityPlanes.scope: Create conditions for speaking up, shared understanding, bounded delegation, coordinated action, and team learning.
outcomes: Shared models of goals, roles, and constraints
Faster recovery and learning after action
exclusions: Psychological safety as comfort or consensus

capabilityPlanes.title: Design, market & operate
capabilityPlanes.scope: Translate insight into useful experiences, experiments, customer decisions, sales behavior, flow, and reliable operations.
outcomes: Causal learning instead of attribution theater
Visible work-in-progress, constraints, and recovery paths
exclusions: Optimization that ignores customer or system harm

patternIntelligenceLoop.question: What happened, and what can be distinguished from interpretation?
Which features, actors, constraints, and outcomes describe the case?
Which cases share structure, and where do their boundary conditions differ?
What mechanism could explain the pattern, and what would falsify it?
What meaningfully different options follow from the hypothesis?
What smallest safe action can discriminate among the live explanations?
How should roles, triggers, metrics, and exceptions make the learning repeatable?
What differed from the prediction, what failed, and what must change?

evidence.label: Unverified
evidence.definition: Unsourced idea or hypothesis with no external evidence anchor.

evidence.label: Preliminary
evidence.definition: Practitioner account, case, expert description, correlational signal, or early research.

evidence.label: Supported
evidence.definition: A relevant peer-reviewed study or coherent but bounded body of evidence.

evidence.label: Synthesized
evidence.definition: A systematic review, meta-analysis, replicated program, validated construct, or recognized standard.

evidence.label: Convergent
evidence.definition: Multiple high-quality syntheses or standards converge and material counterevidence is addressed.

field.label: Untested
field.definition: No PatternOS field observation has been recorded.

field.label: Observed once
field.definition: One dated use or anecdotal outcome has been recorded with caveats.

field.label: Repeated
field.definition: Repeated use in one context has been recorded without a credible comparison.

field.label: Instrumented
field.definition: Predeclared measures exist across multiple teams, cohorts, or comparable contexts.

field.label: Longitudinal
field.definition: Comparative or longitudinal outcomes and adverse cases have independent review.

transfer.label: Untested
transfer.definition: Transfer beyond the originating context has not been tested.

transfer.label: Near
transfer.definition: The pattern has been tested in a closely similar task or population.

transfer.label: Adjacent
transfer.definition: The invariant has been tested in adjacent domains or materially different teams.

transfer.label: Distant
transfer.definition: The invariant has been tested in dissimilar domains including a human–AI workflow.

rights.label: Allowed in scope
rights.definition: The recorded use is original, licensed, public-domain, or limited to lawful linking, embedding, or short attributed paraphrase.

rights.label: Restricted
rights.definition: Metadata and original commentary are allowed but reproduction or transformation is limited.

rights.label: Permission required
rights.definition: The proposed excerpt, media, transcript, or adaptation needs documented permission.

rights.label: Prohibited
rights.definition: The proposed use is disallowed, unsafe, or incompatible with its license.

drills.title: Contrast-to-transfer sprint
drills.purpose: Practice extracting a bounded invariant from contrasting cases and testing it on a live decision without surrendering judgment to AI.
steps: Choose one consequential but reversible decision and one observable outcome.
Independently write three analogous cases: a success, a failure, and a near miss; do not open AI output yet.
Ask AI for three blind analogues and one counterexample, then reveal and compare the two sets.
Align actors, constraints, actions, feedback, and outcomes; name one candidate invariant and two boundaries.
Generate at least three structurally different moves before evaluating any of them.
Record the predicted result, confidence, falsifier, and decision threshold.
Run the smallest safe test or simulation that distinguishes the options.
Debrief the prediction error and revise or reject the invariant.
scoring: 0–2: comparison uses relational rather than surface similarity
0–2: at least two material boundary conditions are named
0–2: prediction, confidence, and falsifier were recorded before feedback
0–2: the resulting revision changes the pattern, protocol, or next test
stopConditions: The test could cause irreversible harm
Required consent or authority is absent
Cases contain sensitive data that cannot be minimized
No observable outcome can be named

protocols.title: Bounded human–AI decision sprint
protocols.purpose: Use AI to expand and challenge a consequential decision while keeping criteria, authority, consent, and irreversible actions under human control.
roles: Human owner: frames stakes, approves criteria, judges, and remains accountable
Human or AI proposer: creates distinct options
Independent critic: tests options against fixed criteria and failure cases
AI recorder: timestamps predictions, sources, exceptions, and revisions
sequence: Human owner defines the decision, protected values, stakeholders, time horizon, and reversible boundary.
Human owner records an independent view, prediction, and confidence before model output.
Proposer generates structurally distinct options and labels assumptions and required evidence.
Critic receives the decision criteria and examines failure cases without being told the favored option when feasible.
AI recorder renders agreements, conflicts, source gaps, rights limits, and residual uncertainty.
Human owner selects, rejects, or requests another test and states the rationale.
Only reversible approved steps execute; irreversible or high-impact actions enter explicit review.
After the outcome window, owner and recorder compare prediction to result, log exceptions, and revise the chain.
authorityGates: Human approval is required for changes to goals, values, audiences, permissions, or success criteria
Human approval is required before publishing, purchasing, deleting, sending externally, or handling sensitive personal data
The protocol must stop when uncertainty crosses the declared threshold or rollback is unavailable
protocols.exceptionPolicy: Pause the affected action, preserve a minimal factual record, notify the named human owner, propose reversible recovery options, and resume only after the boundary or protocol is explicitly revised.
